FROMLIST: intel_idle: Add S0ix validation This adds validation of S0ix entry and enables it on Skylake. Using the new tick_set_freeze_event function, we program the CPU to wake up X seconds after entering freeze. After X seconds, it will wake the CPU to check the S0ix residency counters and make sure we entered the lowest power state for suspend-to-idle. It exits freeze and reports an error to userspace when the SoC does not enter S0ix on suspend-to-idle. One example of a bug that can prevent a Skylake CPU from entering S0ix (suspend-to-idle) is a leaked reference count to one of the i915 power wells. The CPU will not be able to enter Package C10 and will therefore use about 4x as much power for the entire system. The issue is not specific to the i915 power wells though. BUG=b:62787356 TEST=apply all patches and verify the S0ix check works (is invoked and fails / passes as per the expectations) (Applied from https://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/9148999/) Change-Id: Ic14a569f2d6837750f2ec8bd778d5550809c94f0 Signed-off-by: Derek Basehore <dbasehore@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/557896 Commit-Ready: Rajat Jain <rajatja@chromium.org> Tested-by: Rajat Jain <rajatja@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Rajat Jain <rajatja@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: x86/intel_pmc_core: Add API to provide debug info Some platforms fail to enter suspend-to-idle (S0ix) at times with no access to any debug info. This patch adds an API that can provide information about the state of the PCH IP(s) (ON/OFF) at the moment. This can be used to identify IP(s) that have unexpected ON state (where the system expects them to be OFF) thus causing S0ix entry failures. CNL: Use SYS_RST_L for warm/cold chipset reset. The EC cannot control warm vs cold reset of the chipset using the SYS_RST_L pin; it's just a reset request. This commit changes the behaviour of chipset_reset to assert SYS_RST_L regardless if a cold or a warm reset is requested. Fix activate date with correct deps and wait time This script had multiple race conditions that would cause silent failures. However, since there are no tests for this setup and it only ever needs to succeed once, the race conditions were never caught. The first condition was a dependency to tlsdated, which if the service hadn't started yet, when the dbus message was sent, it would fail and cause an early termination of the script. The second was a sleep 200, which causes sleep for 200 seconds, which eventually causes a timeout during init and this process is killed. This sets the deps correctly and changes the sleep to 2 seconds when waiting for the network time to be set correctly. Autotest system tests will be added on a subsequent change to test the overall activate setup. BUG=chromium:748153 TEST=tested locally on pryo Change-Id: I5126d6b084490d62d9ddaecb53d1c2f0879ca5a7 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/583772 Commit-Ready: C Shapiro <shapiroc@google.com> Tested-by: C Shapiro <shapiroc@google.com> Reviewed-by: Simon Glass <sjg@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Jason Clinton <jclinton@chromium.org>
